newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Caribbean vows to fight for EU banana deal.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean vows to fight for EU banana deal.

text.p: Caribbean leaders Thursday vowed they would fight to save a preferential banana export agreement with the European Union, which has been under assault from U.S.-backed producers in Central America.

In May, the World Trade Organization upheld Washington's complaint that the EU discriminated against giant U.S. and Central American banana growers in favor of Europe's traditional suppliers in Africa, the Pacific and Caribbean, including the tiny nations of the Caribbean Community.

Some island leaders attending Caricom's summit this week have accused the United States of hypocrisy for what they see as Washington's efforts to damage an important industry at the same time it is pressuring them to sign treaties that allow U.S. drug agents to enter their territories.

"If big powers can break rules with impunity asserting security interests, and are free to threaten our security interests, for that is what bananas comes down to, something in wrong with the WTO," Shridath Ramphal, Caricom's chief trade negotiator, said.
Caricom leaders at the summit met Thursday with EU commissioner Joao Pinheiro to coordinate strategies on the EU appeal of the ruling.

They also said the regional organization will send a delegation to next week's summit of Central American leaders in Panama to press their case, and could hold more talks with the United States as well.

In May, President Clinton told Caribbean leaders during a meeting in Barbados that he would not push for immediate implementation of the WTO ruling, but instead would try to negotiate a settlement with the EU that would minimize any harm to the Caribbean.
But Edson James, Dominica's prime minister, said he was disappointed with a U.S. request for more talks with the Caribbean and failure to make any proposals.

"We're now back to square one," he said. "We've gone that road before, we're just going around in circles...but we've not ruled out any Seven of the 14 Caricom member-states rely on banana exports for a significant portion of their total earnings. In the four Windward Island states of Dominica, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and Grenada, bananas are the main export earner.
Grenada Prime Minister Keith Mitchell said that Caricom needed time to diversify its agriculture production and to find alternate markets for its bananas.
"We need the appeal to give ourselves sufficient time to diversify," he said. "I think that is going to determine whether we succeed or fail."
